In this World Cup finals, over 23%, nearly a quarter of the players were not born in the country they represent, with both the proportion and number of players reaching a record high. Among the 48 teams, eight squads have a majority of players born outside their country. The Netherlands' constituent country in the Caribbean, Curaçao, with a population smaller than that of Wan Chai, has only the most valuable player, Sheffield United's Cantonese descendant Tahith Chong, born locally, with all other players coming from the Netherlands itself. Second only to Curaçao and the Democratic Republic of Congo, the African leader Morocco with the third-highest number of foreign-born players set a World Cup record in their first group match against Brazil, with all 11 players on the pitch not born in the country.

The David and Goliath contrast at the World Cup is not only about the fans' viewing perspective, but also about FIFA's struggle to simultaneously leverage popular star players and underdog nations to boost attention. This tournament has been plagued by controversies, with fans mocking star players being promoted as "FIFA Boys," and multiple national teams submitting post-match appeals to FIFA regarding refereeing standards. These all reflect that while FIFA's revenue from this World Cup has hit a record high, the true most important participants in the game have seen their confidence in the conflict-of-interest-ridden host plummet to rock bottom.

For fans, when they recall the classic matches of the 2026 World Cup in the future, it may not be the final, but rather the thrilling 3-2 knockout round match between defending champions Argentina and Cape Verde. The previously unknown 40-year-old Cape Verdean goalkeeper Vozinha became an overnight sensation by consecutively saving shots from football king Messi, and has now become a world-renowned star with nearly 30 million followers. As a player born in a small country, being able to compete on equal footing with legendary stars on the world's biggest sports stage through skill is the true charm of the World Cup. Cape Verde defender Lupu, who almost missed the call-up, said after the match: "One of the best things about this World Cup is that no one asks where Cape Verde is on the map anymore. For us, this is making history. We have put ourselves on the map."

考慮將參賽球隊增至64隊

Ahead of the previous World Cup, FIFA wrote to all participating teams, earnestly requesting them to "let football be the protagonist" and not allow football to be drawn into any ideological or political struggles. At that time, the World Cup was still hosted by a single country and featured 32 national teams. The next World Cup will celebrate its centennial and will be held across three continents and six countries in an unprecedented arrangement. After a series of controversies, as this World Cup enters its final stretch, President Gianni Infantino said he would consider expanding the number of participating teams to 64, describing the World Cup as "for the whole world." Amid a changing world, the saying that "the ball is round" ignites unprecedented hope for global audiences every four years, but only with a fair playing environment can victory truly belong to football and to you.
